title: Introduce staged-eager prefilter and deterministic tail-capture to eliminate hotpath allocations
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: The current trace instrumentation performs several heap allocations and field serializations on the request hotpath even when the request will not be retained by sampling rules. This increases tail latency variance and adds CPU pressure on high-QPS inference endpoints. Goal: Reduce hotpath allocations and per-request overhead while preserving high-fidelity tail capture for posthoc debugging. Approach: 1) Add a two-stage 'staged-eager prefilter' that performs an extremely cheap signature check and tokenization within the hotpath (zero allocations or stack-only), and promotes only a compact sampling token to the rest of the runtime. 2) When the prefilter signals a candidate for tail capture, instead of allocating full span objects immediately, emit a deterministic sampling token and a tiny inline event (<=64 bytes) to the trace ingress. A background deterministic tail-capture worker will rehydrate full spans by replaying the minimal events with deterministic ordering and fixed-size slab buffers. 3) Use a memguard slab allocator (per-shard, small fixed-size pool) and zero-copy metadata references in the ingress to avoid transient allocations during background enrichment. 4) Make sampling decisions reproducible by using a per-tenant seed + request-hash to allow idempotent background replay and to correlate log/metric artifacts without attaching full spans on the hotpath. Note: this is intentionally conservative — background rehydration is performed off the critical path and is bounded by a configurable window. Trade-offs: - Slight increase in complexity and operational surface (tail-capture worker, slab sizes, replay invariants). - Potential delayed visibility of full-span traces until background rehydration completes (should be acceptable for posthoc debugging). - Deterministic hashing fixes flakiness but requires careful versioning to avoid cross-release mismatches.
acceptance_criteria: Hotpath per-request heap allocations for instrumentation reduced by >=40% in microbenchmark compared to baseline
P95 latency regression on ingress path <= +1ms; P99 regression <= +3ms
End-to-end tail trace rehydration succeeds for 99% of sampled candidates in staging replay tests
Shadow-run telemetry shows no increase in dropped traces and background worker CPU remains within 10% of target capacity
PRs merged with unit + integration tests; rollout runbook and rollback steps documented

updates: 2026-01-27: Kickoff meeting with runtime and observability. Agreed on two-stage approach and memguard slab idea.
2026-02-05: Prototype prefilter implemented in local runtime branch (no copy path). Initial microbenchmarks show ~30% allocation reduction and unchanged P50.

2026-02-24: Background worker prototype ready; initial replay logic can reconstruct spans 94% of the time in synthetic traces. Missing cases traced to non-deterministic header ordering — fixed by canonical header sort.
2026-02-28: PR opened for prefilter and token wire format: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4712 — awaiting security review and perf CI results.

2026-03-01: Perf CI run (staging) shows 42% reduction in hotpath allocations and P99 latency down 0.6ms on the hotpath; ready for canary planning. Noted one regression: worker memory high for tenant with 3k concurrent rehydrates — adding per-tenant cap.
